mike: Heads-up: after the 'vec-pref' kernel selector rollout in canary-2026-03-23 I'm seeing host-side tail regressions on the rtx pool. P95 ingress parse/tokenize up ~15%.

elaine: Any flamegraphs or syscall profiles?

mike: Quick perf capture (30s) attached, top of stack looks like:
```
parse.ingress.read_loop +42%
  |-- grpc::stream_read_frame +26%
  |-- tokenize_worker::tokenize_batch +14%
syscall profile: many repeated writev/readv pairs with 8-24B frames
```
KV cache metrics are flat (miss rate ~= baseline). Batching medians dropped from 5->2 after selector preferred vec for <80 tokens.

rob: That rings a bell. Vec kernel reduces GPU per-seq latency but increases sensitivity to host batching windows. If batch size collapses, we end up with many small frames and syscall churn.

toni: Can reproduce locally with a stress harness. Short summary of quick ablation:
- force-vec: p95 host parse +16%
- force-legacy: p95 host parse baseline
- enable-proxy-coalesce: p95 host parse -9% vs force-vec
(so host coalescing at the proxy regained most of the win)

mike: Nice. Can you paste the microbench commands?

toni: Sure:
```bash
# spawn 2000 concurrent tiny requests against canary
./stress_client --concurrency 2000 --prompt-size 12 --duration 60 --target canary-rtx
# capture syscalls per request
sudo perf record -F 99 -a -g -- sleep 60
perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl | ./flamegraph.pl > /tmp/flame.svg
```

elaine: Two mitigation lanes: short-term proxy coalescer (coalesce small writes for 10-15ms or until N bytes) + expose backend batching timeout knob; medium-term: expose an explicit contract from kernel selector about expected host_frame_size so the host can adapt batching heuristics.

rob: I also prototyped a socket-level tweak: setting TCP_CORK + writev aggregation in the sidecar reduced syscall wakeups by ~70% for tiny frames. But TCP_CORK has tradeoffs on latency for long-payload requests. We should only enable when small_write_rate > threshold.

perf-bot: Canary run summary id=canary-1901234567-01: 10k requests sampled. Metrics:
- end2end P95: +13% vs baseline
- host parse P95: +15%
- median batch size: 5 -> 2
- syscall wakeups/request: 1.1 -> 3.2
Results uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/canaries/1901234567-01/

mike: Thanks. Action items:
1) Toni to open a PR for proxy coalescer (opt-in flag + small-write-rate metric) - quick patch for canary.
2) Elaine to add kernel-selector hint API (host_frame_hint param) to selector interface spec.
3) Rob to add a guarded TCP_CORK experiment into sidecar (feature flag).
4) Add alert: `host_small_write_rate > 500/s` triggers auto-fallback to legacy selector for that pool.

elaine: I'll draft the selector hint API doc today, linking expected host_frame_size to batching_timeout heuristics.

toni: PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/9999 (WIP) -- simple coalescer added behind a flag `--coalesce-small-writes` ; testing now.

mike: Short-term plan approved. If we can get the proxy coalescer into the canary quickly we may avoid rolling back the vec pref. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
